rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Cards 4 Variations Overview This is a co-operative game to beat the Queen and fill the garden before she catches up and beheads you all! Turn On your turn, pick a tile to place on the grid. This new tile will then be filled with player cubes. For each player, those cubes show how many adjacent tiles can combine with the new tile to match the player's secret card. To determine the number of cubes, first check to see if the new tile matches either half of your card. If the new tile does not match either half of a player's secret card, a cube showing "0" will be placed for that player. If the tile does match one half, imagine placing the card onto the board, and rotating it. How many adjacent tiles make a perfect match with the secret card? NB: It's based on tiles, not symbols. This means that 2 heart-pink tiles side-by-side will still only mean 1 match with a heart-pink card. The group then has to make at least one guess, but may make more. However, be warned, if an incorrect guess is made, the Queen races at you at double speed. If a correct guess is made, and the group chooses to stop, the queen moves at single speed which is equal to the number of flower tokens she holds (starts with 1, but gains an extra each time the team token passes a rabbit space). For the player(s) who had their card correctly guessed by the others, it has a number on it to show how far your team token will move (Easy cards are pretty short, and Hard cards are pretty long). Each player whose card was correctly guessed may now take a new card of a difficulty of their choosing. Cards Green Easy cards are always only two colours, but only ONE member of the team may hold a card of this type at one time. When correctly guessed, this has the potential of 1-2 movement spaces. The Easy deck contains 2 each of 10 combinations. Blue Medium cards are either two colours OR two shapes. When correctly guessed, this has the potential of 2-3 movement spaces. The Medium deck contains 2 each of 20 combinations. Red Hard cards are either two colours OR two shapes OR 1 Colour & 1 Shape. When correctly guessed, this has the potential of 4-5 movement spaces. The Hard deck contains 2 each of 36 combinations. End of the Game You and your teammates win if the royal garden is filled without the Gardeners being caught by the Queen. Note: Players must still complete all phases of a turn, including guessing a Whim and moving the Queen, even on the turn the garden is fully filled. You and your teammates immediately lose the game if the Queen reaches or passes the Gardeners on the score track. The Queen’s cry, “Off with their heads!” is heard around the palace grounds. Variations The two player variation includes "Clue" tokens which can be used to SKIP the Guess a Whim Card phase causing the Queen to move as if the whim had been correctly guessed, but the Gardeners don't move at all.

[Rating: 1/10] this is not a strategy or logic deduction game. Your clues have to depend on what's available in the greenhouse. If you want to be true to the theme, Alice should be able to escape once she runs around the garden and reaches the gate.

[Rating: 1/10] Scored at 1 because of massive production flaws on Deluxe. 5mm lid lift is inexcusable especially with game trays.  Actual ranking would be around a 4 anyhow. Game is far too punishing to be enjoyable. It’s super approachable other than the difficulty curve for failing.

[Rating: 2/10] There is no skill or challenge here. It's literally just a process of eliminating possibilities. All we did was take notes each round until we knew the answer, and then repeat the process, there was never any pressure or feeling that we might lose the game.  I could see how, in theory, there is some skill involved in picking the best hint, but there isn't enough incentive to focus on that. Theoretically, if we don't pick good hints the queen could catch up, but she never got close in our game.   In the end, this game just felt like tedious paperwork. [Rating: 2/10] (Played at 2p; don't recommend with 2)  Deduction game where you are playing tiles to clue your partners on goal cards you're holding. You put cubes on the placed tile based on the number of matches of your goal appear on it. I think that mechanically the game had a good idea, but the game is so oddly tight that there is no breathing room at all, and thus no room for cleverness. I feel like this should have been better. That said, I did actually have to try and pigeonhole with marking the board and doing process of elimination at one point. Too linear of an experience though.

[Rating: 3/10] It seems like this game requires too many wild guesses.   Looking in to which tiles are left in the greenhouse and where all available placement options are only gets you so far. When I watch gameplay videos of this, I see the same thing happening and people seem to enjoy the thrill of those guesses.   Ultimately, I think this game just isn't for me. We played it 2 and 3 player before trading it.

[Rating: 3/10] Actively disliked. Before this game, I had never experienced such a severe drop in excitement to play a game within the first 5 minutes. When you realize you have to fill out the little tracking sheets for almost... every... tile... over... and over again... No, thank you. This was the biggest disappointment I've had with a game in a long time. Beautiful, but little meaningful gameplay and burdensome to play.

[Rating: 3/10] It's not often I rate this low....But a deduction game, based on tiles picked at random ? Come on.... Added to the fact the queen is very aggressive, makes for a game very hard to beat and very dependent on luck. I love deduction games like Turing Machine or Cryptide but this one is clearly missing its target in my opinion.

[Rating: 3/10] [Review] boring and dry coop alice in wonderland euro-game with deduction elements  pros + nice artwork and theme + coop deduction game  cons - visual clarity is an issue - limited and less interesting decisions (where to place a tile, guessing) - luck depended (getting the perfectly fitting tasks or tiles has a huge impact on winning or lossing) - exhausting gameplay (constantly observing and recording data ) - the deduction for me is not satisfying (not thematic) - abstract game

[Rating: 3/10] I was very eager to play this game, watched reviews on youtube, love the theme, but alas ultimately it was a let down. The board is beautiful, figures are nice and detailed, big enough elements to handle comfortably, and very good graphic design. The game is deduction based with three level of difficulty depending on which you pick, apart from that you will need some strategic decisions on which tiles to pick and where to put them.
